subject: science
prompt_en: Count your pulse while sitting quietly: count the beats at your wrist for 30 seconds and double it. Predict: after one minute of skipping or jumping on the spot, will it go up, go down or stay the same? Why?
prompt_hi: Shaanti se baith ke apni nabz gino: kalaai pe 30 second tak dhadkan gino aur do se guna karo. Guess karo: ek minute rassi koodne ya jagah pe uchhalne ke baad nabz badhegi, ghategi ya utni hi rahegi? Kyon?
answer: It goes up, because working muscles need more oxygen and food energy, so the heart pumps faster to deliver them.

subject: science
prompt_en: Predict which breakfast will keep you full and active longer until lunch: a packet of chips with a cola, or poha with peanuts and a glass of milk.
prompt_hi: Guess karo kaunsa nashta tumhe lunch tak zyada der bhara aur active rakhega: chips ka packet aur cola, ya moongfali wala poha aur ek glass doodh.
answer: Poha with peanuts and milk: it gives carbohydrates, protein and some fat that release energy steadily; chips and cola give a quick sugar rush, little nutrition, and hunger again soon.

subject: science
prompt_en: Why are adolescent girls in India at greater risk of anaemia, and what helps?
prompt_hi: Bharat mein kishor ladkiyon ko anaemia ka khatra zyada kyon hota hai, aur kya madad karta hai?
answer: They are growing fast and lose some blood during periods each month, so they need more iron. Iron-rich foods eaten with vitamin C, and iron tablets when a doctor or a school health programme gives them, help.

subject: science
prompt_en: Compare two routines: Raju bathes daily and changes his socks every day; Manu bathes every three days and wears the same socks. Who is more likely to have body odour and skin problems, and why?
prompt_hi: Do routine ki tulna karo: Raju roz nahaata hai aur roz moze badalta hai; Manu 3 din mein ek baar nahaata hai aur wahi moze pehenta hai. Kisko shareer ki gandh aur skin ki pareshaani hone ki zyada sambhavna hai, aur kyon?
answer: Manu, because sweat builds up on his skin and socks and bacteria grow on it, causing odour and skin infections; Raju's daily washing removes the sweat and bacteria.

subject: science
prompt_en: Simran says, 'I'll skip lunch and dinner so I become fit fast.' What is the problem with her plan?
prompt_hi: Simran kehti hai, 'Main lunch aur dinner chhod doongi taaki jaldi fit ho jaaun.' Uske plan mein kya gadbad hai?
answer: Her growing body needs regular, balanced meals; skipping them makes her tired and weak, harms growth and concentration, and is not fitness. Fitness comes from balanced food, daily activity and good sleep.

subject: science
prompt_en: A vegetarian hostel serves rice, aloo sabzi and tea every day. Suggest two changes that would give the students more iron and protein.
prompt_hi: Ek shaakahari hostel mein roz chawal, aloo ki sabzi aur chai milti hai. Do aise badlav sujhao jisse students ko zyada iron aur protein mile.
answer: For example: add dal, chana or rajma for protein and iron; add green leafy vegetables like palak or methi with lemon; give milk, curd or paneer; serve tea away from meals; include millets like bajra or ragi.

subject: science
prompt_en: Design a one-day plan for a Class 7 student that fits in school, homework, play and sleep, and meets the needs of a growing body.
prompt_hi: Class 7 ke ek student ke liye ek din ka plan banao jismein school, homework, khelna aur sona sab ho, aur badhte shareer ki zaroorat poori ho.
answer: It should include three balanced meals and healthy snacks (with dal, vegetables, milk or curd, fruit), about an hour of active play, around 9 or more hours of sleep, a daily bath and brushing twice, and limited screen time.

subject: science
prompt_en: Draw a thali divided into parts showing what a growing adolescent's lunch should include. Label one food in each part and what it gives the body.
prompt_hi: Ek thaali banao jo hisson mein bati ho aur dikhaaye ki badhte adolescent ke lunch mein kya hona chahiye. Har hisse mein ek khaana aur wo shareer ko kya deta hai, label karo.
answer: For example: roti or rice (energy), dal, chana, paneer or egg (protein), green leafy sabzi (iron and vitamins), curd (calcium), salad or fruit (vitamins and fibre), and a glass of water.

subject: science
prompt_en: Explain to a younger cousin why personal hygiene becomes more important during adolescence, and give two habits to follow.
prompt_hi: Apne chhote cousin ko samjhao ki adolescence mein saaf-safaai zyada zaroori kyon ho jaati hai, aur do aadatein batao.
answer: Sweat and oil glands become more active, so bacteria on sweaty skin cause body odour and skin problems. Habits: bathe daily, wear clean clothes and socks, wash the face gently, brush twice a day, and for girls change pads regularly during periods.

subject: science
prompt_en: From last time: which fruits or vegetables help your body absorb iron from palak?
prompt_hi: Pichhli baar se: kaunse phal ya sabziyan palak ka iron shareer mein lene mein madad karte hain?
answer: Foods rich in vitamin C, such as lemon, amla, guava, orange or tomato.

subject: science
prompt_en: Sort these into good and poor conductors of heat: steel spoon, wooden ladle, aluminium pan, plastic handle, woollen cloth, copper wire.
prompt_hi: Inhe garmi ke acche aur kharaab conductor mein baanto: steel ka chammach, lakdi ki karchhi, aluminium ka pan, plastic ka handle, oon ka kapda, copper ka taar.
answer: Good conductors: steel spoon, aluminium pan, copper wire. Poor conductors: wooden ladle, plastic handle, woollen cloth.

subject: science
prompt_en: Wrap one ice cube in a woollen sweater and leave another unwrapped on a plate in the same room. Predict which one will melt first.
prompt_hi: Ek barf ke tukde ko oon ke sweater mein lapeto aur doosre ko usi kamre mein plate pe khula chhodo. Guess karo kaunsa pehle pighlega.
answer: The unwrapped one melts first. The sweater does not make heat; the air trapped in it slows the room's heat from reaching the ice, so the wrapped one melts more slowly.

subject: science
prompt_en: Ask an adult to pour warm water (not boiling) into a mug. Stand a steel spoon, a plastic spoon and a wooden spoon in it. Predict: after two minutes, which handle will feel warmest?
prompt_hi: Kisi bade se mug mein garam (ubalta hua nahi) paani daalne ko kaho. Usme steel ka, plastic ka aur lakdi ka chammach khada karo. Guess karo: do minute baad kiska handle sabse garam lagega?
answer: The steel spoon's handle, because steel is a good conductor and passes heat up from the water quickly; plastic and wood are poor conductors.

subject: science
prompt_en: Place two equal ice cubes at the same moment: one on a steel plate and one on a wooden chopping board, both at room temperature. Predict which melts faster.
prompt_hi: Do barabar barf ke tukde ek hi samay rakho: ek steel ki plate pe aur ek lakdi ke chopping board pe, dono kamre ke taapmaan pe. Guess karo kaun jaldi pighlega.
answer: The one on the steel plate melts faster: steel conducts heat from the plate and the room into the ice much faster than wood does, even though steel feels colder to touch.

subject: science
prompt_en: Why are a kadhai and a tawa made of iron or aluminium, but their handles made of wood or plastic?
prompt_hi: Kadhai aur tawa lohe ya aluminium ke kyon hote hain, par unke handle lakdi ya plastic ke kyon?
answer: The metal conducts heat quickly from the flame to the food; wood and plastic are poor conductors, so the handle stays cool enough to hold.

subject: science
prompt_en: On a winter morning, the steel railing on the school stairs feels much colder than the wooden bench next to it. Why, if both are at the same temperature?
prompt_hi: Sardi ki subah school ki seedhiyon ki steel railing paas ki lakdi ki bench se bahut zyada thandi lagti hai. Agar dono ka taapmaan same hai, toh aisa kyon?
answer: Steel conducts heat away from your hand much faster than wood does, so your hand loses heat quickly and feels cold, even though both are at the same temperature.

subject: science
prompt_en: Compare a cotton shirt and a woollen sweater on a cold day. Why does the sweater keep you warmer, even though neither makes any heat?
prompt_hi: Thande din pe cotton ki shirt aur oon ke sweater ki tulna karo. Sweater zyada garam kyon rakhta hai, jabki dono mein se koi garmi nahi banata?
answer: The sweater's fluffy fibres trap much more air, and air is a poor conductor, so body heat escapes slowly; the thin cotton shirt traps little air.

subject: science
prompt_en: When you hold an ice-cream cone, your hand gets cold and the ice-cream starts melting. Describe which way heat is flowing.
prompt_hi: Jab tum ice-cream cone pakadte ho, haath thanda hota hai aur ice-cream pighalne lagti hai. Batao garmi kis taraf beh rahi hai.
answer: Heat flows from your warm hand (and the air) into the ice-cream; your hand loses heat and feels cold, and the ice-cream gains heat and melts.

subject: science
prompt_en: In winter, birds often fluff up their feathers. Using the idea of conduction, why does this help them stay warm?
prompt_hi: Sardi mein pakshi aksar apne pankh phula lete hain. Conduction ke idea se samjhao ki isse unhe garam rehne mein madad kyon milti hai.
answer: Fluffing up traps more air between the feathers; air is a poor conductor, so less body heat escapes.

subject: science
prompt_en: Ananya writes: 'The fridge puts cold into the food.' Correct the science.
prompt_hi: Ananya likhti hai: 'Fridge khaane mein thand daal deta hai.' Science ko sahi karo.
answer: The fridge takes heat out of the food: heat flows from the warmer food into the colder inside of the fridge, and the fridge pumps that heat outside, so the food cools.

subject: science
prompt_en: Draw a steel rod with one end dipped in a pot of hot water and three markers stuck along its length. Show with arrows how heat moves, and number the markers in the order they would warm up.
prompt_hi: Ek steel ki rod banao jiska ek sira garam paani ke bartan mein dooba ho aur uski lambaai pe 3 marker lage hon. Teer se dikhao ki garmi kaise chalti hai, aur markers ko us kram mein number do jis kram mein wo garam honge.
answer: Arrows go from the end in the hot water along the rod towards the dry end. The marker nearest the hot water warms first (1), then the middle one (2), then the farthest one (3).

subject: science
prompt_en: Explain to your grandfather why his steel tumbler of hot chai is hard to hold, but a kulhad (clay cup) is easy to hold.
prompt_hi: Apne daada ya naana ko samjhao ki garam chai wala steel ka gilaas pakadna mushkil kyon hota hai, par kulhad pakadna aasaan kyon.
answer: Steel is a good conductor, so heat flows quickly from the chai through the tumbler into his fingers; clay is a poor conductor, so the outside of the kulhad stays cooler.

subject: science
prompt_en: From last time: name one good conductor of heat and one poor conductor of heat.
prompt_hi: Pichhli baar se: garmi ka ek accha conductor aur ek kharaab conductor batao.
answer: Good: a metal such as steel, copper, iron or aluminium. Poor: wood, plastic, wool, clay, cloth or air.

subject: science
prompt_en: When does a sea breeze blow, in the day or at night, and in which direction?
prompt_hi: Sea breeze kab chalti hai, din mein ya raat mein, aur kis disha mein?
answer: During the day, from the sea towards the land.

subject: science
prompt_en: Freeze water with a few drops of food colour to make a coloured ice cube. Gently drop it into a clear glass of warm water. Predict where the coloured water will go as the ice melts.
prompt_hi: Paani mein khaane ka rang daal ke rangeen barf ka tukda jamaao. Use dheere se garam paani ke saaf glass mein daalo. Guess karo barf pighalne pe rangeen paani kahaan jaayega.
answer: The cold coloured water sinks to the bottom, because cold water is heavier (denser) than warm water; the warm water stays above. This sinking and rising is convection.

subject: science
prompt_en: A room has a window near the floor and a ventilator near the ceiling. On a hot day, predict which way air will move through each opening.
prompt_hi: Ek kamre mein zameen ke paas ek khidki hai aur chhat ke paas ek ventilator. Garam din pe guess karo har khule hisse se hawa kis taraf chalegi.
answer: Warm air rises and leaves through the ventilator near the ceiling; cooler air from outside comes in through the lower window.

subject: science
prompt_en: Predict: at 10 at night on a beach in Chennai, which way will the breeze near the ground blow, and why?
prompt_hi: Guess karo: Chennai ke beach pe raat 10 baje zameen ke paas hawa kis taraf chalegi, aur kyon?
answer: From the land towards the sea (a land breeze): at night the land cools faster than the sea, so the air over the warmer sea rises and cooler air from the land moves out to replace it.

subject: science
prompt_en: Why does all the water in a pot on the stove get hot, even though only the bottom of the pot touches the flame?
prompt_hi: Chulhe pe rakhe bartan ka saara paani garam kyon ho jaata hai, jabki sirf bartan ki tali aag ko chhooti hai?
answer: Water at the bottom warms, expands, becomes lighter and rises, while cooler water from the top sinks to be heated; these convection currents mix the heat through all the water.

subject: science
prompt_en: Why is an AC fitted high on the wall, while a room heater works best placed on the floor?
prompt_hi: AC deewar pe oonchaai pe kyon lagta hai, jabki room heater zameen pe rakhne pe sabse accha kaam karta hai?
answer: Cool air from the AC is heavier and sinks, spreading through the room; warm air from a heater on the floor rises and spreads upward, so both set up convection currents that mix the room's air.

subject: science
prompt_en: Compare how heat reaches your hand when (a) you hold it above a cup of hot tea, and (b) you touch the top of a steel spoon resting in hot tea. Name the way of heat transfer in each.
prompt_hi: Tulna karo ki garmi tumhare haath tak kaise pahunchti hai jab (a) tum haath garam chai ke cup ke upar rakhte ho, aur (b) garam chai mein rakhe steel ke chammach ka upar wala hissa chhoote ho. Har ek mein garmi pahunchne ka tareeka batao.
answer: (a) Mostly convection: warm air and steam rise up to your hand. (b) Conduction: heat travels through the metal of the spoon to your fingers.

subject: science
prompt_en: Fishermen in coastal Kerala often sail out to sea early in the morning and return in the afternoon. How could land and sea breezes help their sailboats?
prompt_hi: Kerala ke tatiya ilaakon ke machhuaare aksar subah jaldi samudra mein jaate hain aur dopahar ko laut-te hain. Land breeze aur sea breeze unki naav ki kaise madad kar sakti hai?
answer: The land breeze that blows from land to sea through the night and early morning helps push boats out; the afternoon sea breeze blowing from sea to land helps bring them back.

subject: science
prompt_en: Kitchen exhaust fans are fixed high on the wall, and many old houses had openings near the roof of the kitchen. Explain why.
prompt_hi: Kitchen ke exhaust fan deewar pe oonchaai pe lagte hain, aur kai purane gharon mein kitchen ki chhat ke paas khule hisse hote the. Kyon?
answer: Hot air, steam and smoke from cooking rise; openings high up let them escape, while cooler fresh air comes in lower down, keeping the kitchen cooler and less smoky.

subject: science
prompt_en: Dev says, 'Heat only moves up, so the floor next to a heater can't get warm.' What is wrong?
prompt_hi: Dev kehta hai, 'Garmi sirf upar jaati hai, isliye heater ke bagal ka farsh garam nahi ho sakta.' Kya galat hai?
answer: Heat flows from hot to cold in all directions; the heater warms things beside it and below it by radiation and conduction. Only the warm air rises by convection.

subject: science
prompt_en: Draw two pictures of a beach, one for the afternoon and one for the night. Use arrows to show air rising, sinking and moving across, and label which is the sea breeze and which is the land breeze.
prompt_hi: Beach ki do picture banao, ek dopahar ki aur ek raat ki. Teer se dikhao hawa kahaan upar uth rahi hai, kahaan neeche aa rahi hai aur kahaan aar-paar chal rahi hai, aur label karo kaunsi sea breeze hai aur kaunsi land breeze.
answer: Afternoon: air rises over the hot land, sinks over the cooler sea, and near the ground moves from sea to land (sea breeze). Night: air rises over the warmer sea, sinks over the cooler land, and near the ground moves from land to sea (land breeze).

subject: science
prompt_en: Explain convection to a younger child using the coloured ice cube experiment.
prompt_hi: Rangeen barf wale experiment se ek chhote bachche ko convection samjhao.
answer: When the coloured ice melts, the cold coloured water sinks because it is heavier, and warmer water stays on top or rises; liquids and gases carry heat by moving like this, and that is convection.

subject: science
prompt_en: From last time: why does land heat up faster than the sea during the day?
prompt_hi: Pichhli baar se: din mein zameen samudra se jaldi garam kyon hoti hai?
answer: Land (soil and rock) heats up and cools down faster than water, which needs much more heat to warm up and also mixes the heat deep down.

subject: science
prompt_en: Which colour of clothes is better to wear on a hot summer afternoon, and why?
prompt_hi: Garmi ki dopahar mein kis rang ke kapde pehenna behtar hai, aur kyon?
answer: Light colours such as white, because they reflect more sunlight and absorb less heat.

subject: science
prompt_en: Take two identical steel tumblers with the same amount of water. Wrap one in black cloth and one in white cloth, and keep both in the sun for 30 minutes. Predict which water will be warmer.
prompt_hi: Barabar paani wale do ek jaise steel ke gilaas lo. Ek ko kaale kapde mein aur ek ko safed kapde mein lapeto, aur dono ko 30 minute dhoop mein rakho. Guess karo kiska paani zyada garam hoga.
answer: The water in the black-wrapped tumbler, because black cloth absorbs more of the Sun's radiation.

subject: science
prompt_en: Put one ice cube on a sheet of black paper and another on a sheet of white paper in the sun. Predict which melts first.
prompt_hi: Ek barf ka tukda kaale kaagaz pe aur doosra safed kaagaz pe dhoop mein rakho. Guess karo kaunsa pehle pighlega.
answer: The one on black paper, because the black paper absorbs more sunlight, warms up and passes heat into the ice.

subject: science
prompt_en: On a spacewalk, an astronaut's suit faces the Sun on one side. There is no air in space. Predict: will the side of the suit facing the Sun get hot?
prompt_hi: Spacewalk ke dauraan astronaut ke suit ka ek hissa Sun ki taraf hai. Space mein hawa nahi hai. Guess karo: kya suit ka Sun wala hissa garam hoga?
answer: Yes, very hot, because radiation travels through empty space; that is why spacesuits are white and reflective, to reflect much of it.
